items.text: No Kings rallies against President Trump were held Saturday in cities across the U.S., this time urging people to vote early in the Nov. 3 midterms.
items.detail: The anti-Trump No Kings network, which has staged several nationwide protest days over the past year, billed Saturday's "No Kings: Vote Early" events as a day of voter participation, with registration and early-voting information tables, rather than purely a protest. In Washington, marchers crossed Memorial Bridge from Arlington, Virginia, to the Lincoln Memorial. Organizers said events were planned in all 50 states.
items.why: The movement behind some of the largest anti-Trump protests is now turning its turnout toward the midterm elections, about two weeks away.

items.text: France's nationwide protests over rising living costs turned violent Saturday, with cars burned and shops looted in Paris and at least 272 people arrested.
items.detail: Tens of thousands marched in cities across France, joining weeks of high-school student protests. In Paris, police used tear gas and water cannons on masked protesters around Place de la République. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's office reported a growing number of violent incidents nationwide, including assaults on officers, looting and damage to public buildings; protesters broke into town halls in Marseille and Lille, and the tourist office in Lyon was set on fire. The arrest count is the government's tally as of Saturday afternoon and may rise.
items.why: Weeks of student unrest have widened into one of France's most violent protest days in years, as its presidential campaign takes shape.

items.text: Kenya's Ebola cases rose to seven, including three health workers who cared for the country's first patient, the Health Ministry said Saturday.
items.detail: The four new cases are the three health workers, who treated the first patient Oct. 3-4 and had been in quarantine since Oct. 9, and a close male relative of that patient, in quarantine since Oct. 6. All four developed fever before testing positive and are in isolation receiving care. The total includes the first patient, who died in Nairobi. The ministry said the outbreak is the Bundibugyo strain, 128 of 130 known contacts have been traced, and there is no evidence of community spread; it called the risk to the public low.
items.why: Infections among caregivers show Ebola spreading inside Kenya, East Africa's main travel hub.

items.text: Pakistani and Afghan Taliban forces exchanged fire Saturday on the border in Pakistan's Upper Kurram district, Pakistan's state media said.
items.detail: Pakistan's state broadcaster said Afghan forces opened fire first, to help militants cross the border, and that the army answered with heavy weapons and destroyed several Afghan posts. Pakistani security sources said several Taliban personnel were killed; neither side's casualty claims have been independently confirmed. The district sits opposite Afghanistan's Paktia province. The two countries have clashed repeatedly since border fighting in October 2025, and Pakistan carried out airstrikes inside Afghanistan on Oct. 1.
items.why: Fighting between two neighbors, one nuclear-armed, keeps flaring along a border Pakistan says militants use to attack it.

items.text: A second oil tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed Saturday; no one has independently confirmed it.
items.detail: Iran's official IRNA news agency said both tankers, each carrying about 2 million barrels of crude, caught fire after striking naval mines and the second was left immobilized, and that they had switched off tracking and used a route Iran had not authorized. The Guards did not name either ship. This updates this morning's report of the first claimed mine strike.
items.why: Iran is escalating claims of mine attacks on the world's main oil route, with Brent crude near $110.

items.text: European diplomats visiting the occupied West Bank during the olive harvest were attacked by masked Israeli settlers, and Israeli police opened an investigation.
items.detail: The delegation, near the Palestinian village of Taybeh outside Ramallah, included Belgium's consul general, French and Polish diplomats and Catholic church representatives. A window of a Belgian consulate vehicle was smashed and a French mayor traveling with the group was assaulted. Israeli police said they opened the probe after footage circulated online and would work to identify the suspects. Palestinian officials say at least four Palestinians have been killed and more than 100 injured since the harvest began this month.
items.why: An attack on foreign diplomats raises pressure on Israel from European governments over settler violence.

items.text: Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli Hospital and returned to the Vatican on Saturday, four days after surgery that removed part of his right lung for cancer.
items.detail: His doctors, Dr. Luigi Carbone and Prof. Stefano Margaritora, said blood tests and a chest X-ray Saturday morning showed he was fit to be discharged. The Holy See Press Office said he will lead the Angelus prayer from the Apostolic Palace on Sunday. Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni said recovery is expected to take about a week; his schedule is cleared until at least Oct. 20, and the Vatican has not announced further treatment. His next major trip, to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, is set for early November.
items.why: The leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics is back at work sooner than expected after a lung cancer operation.

upcoming.text: Comment deadline on Treasury's proposed GENIUS Act stablecoin rules.
upcoming.detail: Treasury's proposal sets how the GENIUS Act's limits on issuing, offering and selling payment stablecoins in the U.S. would work. Final rules come later.

upcoming.text: Comment deadline on the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets.
upcoming.detail: The proposal would add a safe harbor under which some crypto assets would not be treated as investment contracts under securities law. The SEC must still vote on a final rule.
